tagline.en: Who, which, that: join two ideas
tagline.bn: Who, which, that দিয়ে দুটি ভাবনা জোড়ো

subtitle.en: Every card has a short rule and 3 questions. Join two short sentences into one with who, which, that, where and whose.
subtitle.bn: প্রতিটি কার্ডে ছোট্ট নিয়ম আর ৩টি প্রশ্ন। who, which, that, where, whose দিয়ে দুটি ছোট বাক্যকে একটিতে জোড়ো।

hint.en: When to drop the word, when to add commas

rule.en: Use who to give more information about a person.
rule.bn: কোনো মানুষ সম্পর্কে আরও তথ্য দিতে who।

recap.example: the girl who sings · a man who teaches

questions.prompt: That’s the doctor ___ helped me.

options.why: which is for things. A doctor is a person.
where is for places.
whose shows belonging, but nothing belongs to anyone here.

questions.prompt: I have a friend ___ in Chattogram.

options.why: a friend is one person, so use lives.
A friend is a person: who.
Don’t add he. who already stands for the friend.

questions.prompt: Join: I met a boy. He plays cricket.

options.text: I met a boy who plays cricket.
I met a boy who he plays cricket.
options.why: who replaces he, so drop he.

options.text: I met a boy which plays cricket.
options.why: A boy is a person: who.

options.text: I met a boy, he plays cricket.
options.why: A comma can’t join two sentences. Use who.

rule.en: Use which or that for things and animals. that can also be used for people.
rule.bn: বস্তু ও প্রাণীর জন্য which বা that। that মানুষের জন্যও চলে।

recap.example: the book which I bought · a phone that works

questions.prompt: This is the bag ___ I lost.

options.why: who is for people. A bag is a thing.
where is for places.
whose shows belonging.

questions.prompt: I like films ___ make me laugh.

options.why: Films are things, so use that or which.
where is for places.
what can’t join a noun to a clause like this. Use that or which.

questions.prompt: Join: She has a cat. It sleeps all day.

options.text: She has a cat that it sleeps all day.
options.why: that replaces it, so drop it.

options.text: She has a cat that sleeps all day.
She has a cat where sleeps all day.
options.why: where is for places.

options.text: She has a cat, sleeps all day.
options.why: You need that or which to join them.

rule.en: Use where after a place and when after a time.
rule.bn: স্থানের পরে where, সময়ের পরে when।

recap.example: the village where I was born · the day when we met

questions.prompt: This is the café ___ we first met.

options.why: A café is a place, not a time.
who is for people.
whose shows belonging.

questions.prompt: I remember the year ___ I started school.

options.why: A year is a time, not a place.
who is for people.
whose shows belonging.

questions.prompt: Join: That’s the hospital. My sister works there.

options.text: That’s the hospital where my sister works there.
options.why: where replaces there, so drop there.

options.text: That’s the hospital where my sister works.
That’s the hospital when my sister works.
options.why: A hospital is a place: where.

options.text: That’s the hospital who my sister works.
options.why: who is for people.

rule.en: whose replaces his, her, their or its. It is always followed by a noun.
rule.bn: whose বসে his, her, their বা its-এর জায়গায়। এর পরে সবসময় একটি noun থাকে।

recap.example: the man whose car was stolen

questions.prompt: She’s the student ___ essay won the prize.

options.why: The essay belongs to her, so use whose.
who’s means who is. Here we need belonging: whose.
which is for things, and we need belonging.

questions.prompt: I know a girl ___ father is a pilot.

options.why: “who father” is wrong. The father belongs to her: whose.
Don’t add her. whose already means her.
that doesn’t show belonging.

questions.prompt: Join: That’s the boy. His bike is red.

options.text: That’s the boy whose his bike is red.
options.why: whose replaces his, so drop his.

options.text: That’s the boy who bike is red.
options.why: Use whose to show the bike is his.

options.text: That’s the boy whose bike is red.
That’s the boy who’s bike is red.
options.why: who’s means who is.

rule.en: You can drop who, which or that when a new subject comes after it. Never add an extra it, him or her.
rule.bn: পরে নতুন subject থাকলে who, which বা that বাদ দিতে পারো। কখনো বাড়তি it, him বা her যোগ করবে না।

recap.example: the cake (that) I made · the man (who) we saw

questions.prompt: In which sentence can you leave out “that”?

options.text: The bus that goes to Mirpur is late.
options.why: that is the subject of goes, so you can’t drop it.

options.text: The film that we watched was good.
The man that lives next door is kind.
options.why: that is the subject of lives, so you can’t drop it.

options.text: The phone that broke was new.
options.why: that is the subject of broke, so you can’t drop it.

questions.explanation: A new subject (we) comes after that, so it can go.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: The book which I bought it is great.
options.why: which already stands for the book. Drop it.

options.text: The book I bought is great.
The book I bought it is great.
options.why: Don’t add it. The book is already named.

options.text: The book what I bought is great.
options.why: Use which or that (or nothing), not what.

questions.explanation: Drop which, and never add it.

questions.prompt: Join without who, which or that: This is the song. I love it.

options.text: This is the song I love it.
options.why: Drop it. The song is already named.

options.text: This is the song what I love.
options.why: Don’t use what here.

options.text: This is the song I loves.
options.why: With I, use love.

options.text: This is the song I love.

cards.badge: My brother, who lives in Dhaka, …

rule.en: If the information is extra, put it between commas and use who or which, never that.
rule.bn: তথ্যটি বাড়তি হলে দুই কমার মাঝে রাখো, আর who বা which ব্যবহার করো, কখনো that নয়।

recap.example: My brother, who lives in Dhaka, is a teacher.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: Dhaka, that is the capital, is very busy.
options.why: Never use that after a comma.

options.text: Dhaka, who is the capital, is very busy.
options.why: Dhaka is a place, not a person.

options.text: Dhaka which is the capital, is very busy.
options.why: Extra information needs two commas.

options.text: Dhaka, which is the capital, is very busy.

questions.prompt: My mother, ___ is a nurse, works at night.

options.why: Never use that after a comma.
which is for things. Your mother is a person.
whose shows belonging.

questions.prompt: Join: The Sundarbans is home to tigers. It is a mangrove forest.

options.text: The Sundarbans, which is a mangrove forest, is home to tigers.
The Sundarbans, that is a mangrove forest, is home to tigers.
options.why: Never use that after a comma.

options.text: The Sundarbans, which it is a mangrove forest, is home to tigers.
options.why: which replaces it, so drop it.

options.text: The Sundarbans which is a mangrove forest is home to tigers.
options.why: This is extra information, so it needs commas.

questions.explanation: Extra information about a place → , which …,

cards.badge: the house I grew up in

rule.en: In everyday English, put the preposition at the end. In formal English, put it before whom or which.
rule.bn: সাধারণ ইংরেজিতে preposition শেষে বসে। আনুষ্ঠানিক ইংরেজিতে whom বা which-এর আগে বসে।

recap.example: the house I grew up in · the person to whom I spoke

questions.prompt: That’s the friend I told you ___.

options.why: You need a preposition at the end: about.
which can’t end the sentence here. You need about.
Don’t add it. You need a preposition: about.

questions.explanation: tell someone about someone → I told you about.

questions.prompt: The chair ___ which you are sitting is very old.

options.why: We sit on a chair, not to it.
We sit on a chair, not of it.
by means next to. You sit on a chair.

questions.explanation: sit on a chair → on which.

questions.prompt: Which is the formal version of “This is the man I spoke to”?

options.text: This is the man to whom I spoke.
This is the man to who I spoke.
options.why: After a preposition, use whom.

options.text: This is the man whom I spoke to him.
options.why: Don’t add him.

options.text: This is the man to that I spoke.
options.why: Never use that after a preposition.

cards.badge: the girl sitting there · made in Korea

rule.en: You can drop who/which + be. Use -ing for an active meaning and V3 for a passive meaning.
rule.bn: who/which + be বাদ দিতে পারো। কর্তা নিজে করলে -ing, কাজটি তার উপর হলে V3।

recap.example: the girl sitting there · a phone made in Korea

questions.prompt: The man ___ by the door is my uncle.

options.why: The sentence already has a main verb (is). Use the short form: standing.
The man is doing the action now: standing.
Say either who is standing, or just standing.

questions.prompt: Most of the cars ___ in Japan are sold abroad.

options.why: Cars don’t make anything. They are made, so use V3.
Use the short form: made.
Say either which are made, or just made.

questions.prompt: Shorten: The bus which is leaving now goes to Sylhet.

options.text: The bus left now goes to Sylhet.
options.why: The bus is doing the action, so use -ing.

options.text: The bus is leaving now goes to Sylhet.
options.why: Drop is too: leaving.

options.text: The bus leaving now goes to Sylhet.
The bus which leaving now goes to Sylhet.
options.why: Drop which and is together.
